newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo says economy developing well.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo says economy developing well.

text.p: A year after he was sacked, Argentina's former economy minister Domingo Cavallo said Sunday the country's economy has developed very much as he predicted.
"The economy is going well, just as I had predicted would happen," Cavallo said in an interview with daily La Nacion.
Asked if Argentina is converting itself into an Asian-style tiger economy of Latin America, Cavallo said: "Argentina already is, together with Chile, a kind of tiger."
"If we look at the performance of the 1990s, growth is impressive, it is of the magnitude achieved by the Asian tigers in the 1960s and 1970s," he said.
Cavallo predicted growth would probably reach eight percent this year.
The former minister said there were still necessary changes required in the economy, such as labor market reforms to help bring down unemployment.

Among policies still needed to reduce the jobless rate, Cavallo said more work was needed in sectors like health and education. He also stressed that policies are needed to support the growth of small and medium-sized companies, so that they in turn will create more jobs.
All the same, he characterized his successor, Roque Fernandez, as "a good administrator".
